element_sources.about: MP7 (matter pack design 8.1): a star's birth cloud holds each element in proportion to how much each kind of source had made where and when it formed. The element rows' origin shares (base-reference) say how the Sun's split; this block says how much each source made for this star, relative to the Sun's, from what the star inherited.

equation.name: How much each kind of source made for this star
equation.formula:
s_massive = 10^(feh + alpha_fe)
s_white_dwarfs = max(0, (10^feh - fe_massive * s_massive) / (1 - fe_massive))
s_low_mass = max(0, (c_o / c_o_sun * s_massive - c_massive * s_massive) / (1 - c_massive))
s_cosmic_rays = 10^feh
s_mergers = r_process_rel

feh.name: iron to hydrogen, dex against the Sun

c_o_sun.name: the Sun's carbon to oxygen (the patch model's)

r_process_rel.name: rapid neutron capture elements to hydrogen, against the Sun

fe_massive.name: share of the Sun's iron made by massive stars

c_massive.name: share of the Sun's carbon made by massive stars

s_white_dwarfs.name: exploding white dwarfs, against the Sun

s_low_mass.name: dying low-mass stars, against the Sun

s_cosmic_rays.name: cosmic rays splitting nuclei, against the Sun

s_mergers.name: merging neutron stars, against the Sun

source.text: Kobayashi, Karakas and Lugaro 2020, The origin of elements from carbon to uranium: oxygen and the alpha elements come from massive stars, iron about half from them and half from exploding white dwarfs, carbon about half from low-mass stars, so [alpha/Fe] measures the massive-star share and C/O the low-mass share
source.where: section 6 and its periodic table of origins

explain.curious: Different kinds of star made different elements. A star born where many massive stars had already exploded, but few white dwarfs, has more oxygen and less iron than the Sun.
explain.science: Each source's yield is scaled against the Sun's: massive stars by 10^([Fe/H]+[alpha/Fe]), white dwarfs by what iron then needs, low-mass stars by what C/O then needs, cosmic rays by 10^[Fe/H], neutron-star mergers by the star's own r-process ratio.

patch_model.about: Default patch envelope (galaxy design 7 and 12, stage G0): a Milky-Way-like disc so systems can be formed before any galaxy exists. Closed-form; every number is a pack default with its source. Arms, bar, local texture and events arrive with G4 and G6.

sources.densities: local systems about 0.08 per cubic parsec (RECONS 10 pc census, Henry et al. 2018); thick to thin 0.12 and halo to thin 0.005 at the midplane (Juric et al. 2008)
sources.scale_lengths: thin 2.6 kpc, thick 2.0 kpc; thin 300 pc and thick 900 pc scale heights (Juric et al. 2008; Bland-Hawthorn and Gerhard 2016)
sources.halo: power-law index 2.8 and flattening 0.64 (Juric et al. 2008)
sources.imf: Kroupa 2001, stars only (0.08 to 150 solar masses)
sources.enrichment: ISM [Fe/H] rises as log10 of 1 - exp(-t/tau); present-day gradient -0.06 dex per kpc (Genovali et al. 2014)
sources.alpha_fe: high-alpha plateau with a knee about 1 Gyr after the first stars, from the delay of type Ia supernovae (Matteucci and Francois 1989)
sources.c_o: solar C/O 0.55 (Asplund et al. 2009), rising with [Fe/H] (Nissen et al. 2014)
sources.mg_si: solar Mg/Si 1.2 by number (Asplund et al. 2009); stellar spread from Adibekyan et al. 2015
sources.cluster: embedded cluster masses dN/dM proportional to M^-2 from 10 to 1e5 solar masses (Lada and Lada 2003 measured it from 50 to 1000, with a drop below 50; the wider range is an extrapolation), so per star proportional to M^-1
sources.fuv: birth-cluster far-ultraviolet field, median about 1000 G0 (Fatuzzo and Adams 2008)
sources.al26: rough: most systems are born with less Al-26 than the Sun had (Gounelle 2015; Lichtenberg et al. 2016). Labelled rough
sources.sfr: Milky Way star formation 1.65 solar masses per year (Licquia and Newman 2015)
sources.ia: type Ia delay-time distribution proportional to 1/t from 40 Myr, 1.3e-3 per solar mass formed (Maoz and Mannucci 2012)
sources.velocity: velocity dispersion proportional to age^0.40, about 50 km/s at 10 Gyr (Holmberg, Nordstrom and Andersen 2009 section 6.3: exponents 0.39 U, 0.40 V, 0.53 W, 0.40 total; arXiv 0811.3982)
sources.rocky: [Fe/H] about -1 as the floor for rocky planets: Johnson and Li 2012 (ApJ 751, 81, doi:10.1088/0004-637X/751/2/81) give [Fe/H]_crit about -1.5 + log10(r / 1 au) and Earth-like planets from discs above 0.1 Z_sun; -1 is that limit at about 3 au, one value for all radii (docs/fudges.md)
sources.sterilising: a supernova within 8 pc can strip an ozone layer (Gehrels et al. 2003)
